name: EMMA
intro: EMMA（Enhanced MultiModal reAsoning）是一个旨在评估多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）有机多模态推理能力的基准测试。它涵盖数学、物理、化学和编程等领域，任务需要跨模态推理，不能仅通过单一模态独立解决。对现有MLLMs的评估显示，在处理复杂多模态和多步推理任务方面存在显著局限性，突显了改进多模态架构和训练范式的必要性。
org: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, Sun Yat-sen University, University of Washington, Microsoft, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
build_method: 已有基准严格过滤, 图像描述消融, 分学科技能分类, 领域专家人工扩充与核验
task_type: 多项选择与开放式多模态推理
eval_feature: 文本加图像描述过滤, RAVEN筛选后补充, 47组编程种子构建, EMMA-mini与完整集分范围评测
scale: 2,788个问题（992个过滤自已有基准，1,796个新构建；2,002道选择题，786道开放题）
build_method_en: Strict benchmark filtering, caption ablation, subject skill taxonomies, expert expansion and verification
eval_feature_en: Text-plus-caption filtering, post-filter RAVEN supplementation, 47-set coding construction, scoped EMMA-mini/full evaluation
intro_en: EMMA (Enhanced MultiModal reAsoning) is a benchmark designed to evaluate the organic multimodal reasoning abilities of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). It covers fields such as mathematics, physics, chemistry, and programming, requiring cross-modal reasoning that cannot be solved by a single modality alone. Evaluations of existing MLLMs reveal significant limitations in handling complex multimodal and multi-step reasoning tasks, highlighting the need to improve multimodal architectures and training paradigms.

drawio_review_note: Disambiguated as Enhanced MultiModal reAsoning and aligned with arXiv:2501.05444v1, official repository 4725995, and HF revision 6c87aec. RAVEN supplements the math branch after the three-model filter rather than passing through it. The independent coding track goes from 47 seed visualizations to 188 images in 47 sets and then 564 questions split 188/188/94/94, followed by manual categorization. EMMA-mini has 100 questions per subject, 400 total; human experts and o1 are evaluated only on mini. Direct and CoT are tested for all listed models except o1 and Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking. The paper reports ground-truth accuracy without an MLLM judge; the fixed release evaluator separately exposes equality/SymPy/numeric comparison and optional --gpt_eval.
